verdicts.quote: Promotion is **automatic**: when a place frees, the first eligible waiting member is booked without a further confirmation step.

Order is **first-come-first-served** by the moment the join was accepted. No priority tiers. ... Two joins arriving together get distinct sequences, decided by the order the service commits them. ... Left out: priority/tier ordering, manual reordering by staff.
Left out (domain rules the request does not state): waitlisting for several overlapping classes; ... None is implemented.
verdicts.missing: Whether a member may wait on overlapping classes at all, and what happens to the other entry when one is promoted.

verdicts.quote: penalties or fees for late cancellation (existing rule, preserved, unknown)
verdicts.missing: Whether a promotion the member did not attend or a promotion close to start counts against the existing no-show/late-cancel policy.

verdicts.quote: books the lowest-sequence eligible waiting member ... **in the same atomic unit as the cancellation** ... promotion is **synchronous with the cancellation** (committed together), so no queue, worker or outbox is introduced
the member is informed they are now booked, class name and start. At minimum the in-app status changes ... notification delivery failure never reverses the promotion ... the failure is logged
Exactly one waiting member is promoted per freed place. ... two cancels freeing two places with one waiter (one promotion, one free place)

all state-changing operations on one class (book, cancel, join, leave, promote, capacity change, expiry) are serialised so that I-1…I-5 hold ... I-2 a member has at most one of {booked booking, waiting entry} per class
Eligibility at promotion: credits/payments/limits/late-cancel fees. Does promotion charge the member? ... PD-7: reuse ordinary booking rules; skip ineligible
verdicts.missing: When payment is taken for a promoted booking and what happens if it fails (left as an open user decision).

verdicts.quote: The waitlist has **no product-imposed length cap**. Request names none; an invented bound is forbidden.
no promotion after start ... an operation at exactly the start instant counts as started (inclusive) ... promotion itself checks `now < start`

if capacity rises from C to C′, then in the same atomic unit the first (C′−booked) eligible waiting members are promoted ... Lowering capacity ... keeps the existing rule of the app (unknown); it never creates or removes waiting entries.
If the class is cancelled by staff (when the app supports that), entries become `closed` and each waiting member is informed using the R-6 channel rules

Waitlist entry: member × class session, `sequence` (monotonic per class, assigned at accept time), status `waiting | promoted | left | skipped | expired | closed`. ... Position ... Derived, never stored independently

at the class start time every `waiting` entry becomes `expired` ... Terminal entries are retained only for as long as and in the same manner as the existing app retains booking history for that class; no longer.
A member sees **their own** position and the **count** of people waiting, never another member's identity.
Do staff need a waitlist roster or removal capability? | Not provided ... Left out: staff removing a member from the waitlist (not requested; G-7).
verdicts.missing: Whether staff can view the waitlist, promote or remove by hand, and see promotion history (only logs of waitlist.promoted are stated).

verdicts.quote: **in the same atomic unit as the cancellation** ... No window exists in which the place is free and bookable by a non-waiting member (I-3).
the waitlist action appears only when a class is full; otherwise the unchanged booking action is shown. Booking a class that is not full never creates a waiting entry.
*migration* n/a (new records only, no existing data changed, but see G-1 for schema change in the existing store)
verdicts.missing: Whether classes already full at launch gain a waitlist and how existing full classes are handled at ship time.
